job.title: Credit Controller
job.description:
Credit Controller
Role: Credit Controller
Salary: Up to £48,000
Location: London
Contract: Permanent

Are you an experienced Credit Controller from a law firm or professional services background looking for your next step with a firm that genuinely invests in its people? A highly regarded City law firm, known for advising on some of the most complex and demanding mandates in the market, is looking to add a Credit Controller to its Finance department. This is a newly created position resulting from growth, offering the chance to join a collaborative, supportive team where your contribution will be recognised.

The Role
Sitting within a well established Revenue team and reporting to the Head of Revenue, the Credit Controller will take a proactive approach to supporting collections across the firm. This is a busy and varied role covering large client group debts, a portfolio of aged debts and the monitoring of legal proceedings on unrecoverable debts, as well as complex billing matters, all working towards the firm's cash collection targets. The firm places real emphasis on learning and development, so you will be supported to keep building your skills. Key responsibilities include:
  • Proactively chasing a portfolio of large client group debts to ensure prompt settlement of invoices, including preparing client statements in line with the credit control procedure
  • Organising and attending regular debt meetings with Partners
  • Managing an aged debt portfolio of debts over one year old
  • Taking ownership of issues and queries around unpaid invoices, escalating where necessary, monitoring progress and pursuing until resolved
  • Processing invoice write offs in line with the firm's policies and VAT rules
  • Maintaining a full log of credit control notes and status within the collections application
  • Producing regular debt reports to identify issues for escalation
  • Working with Revenue Controllers to resolve complex debt issues
  • Liaising regularly with Cashiers on the allocation of unapplied or unidentified monies and investigating any errors
  • Where required, preparing and monitoring files for debt recovery on debts deemed unrecoverable
  • Supporting and mentoring junior members of the team, fostering a collaborative, high performance environment
The Candidate
We are looking for someone with:
  • Three to five years' credit control experience, ideally within a law firm, although professional services backgrounds will also be considered
  • Exposure to VAT, disbursements and credit control, with the ability to hit the ground running in a target driven environment
  • Knowledge of Aderant and HighRadius (or other collections software), which would be advantageous
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience of liaising with clients, partners, fee earners, secretaries and finance colleagues
  • A proactive, organised and professional manner, comfortable dealing with stakeholders at all levels of the business
  • A team player who supports and motivates colleagues, follows instructions and is confident to query them when unsure
  • A clear track record of commitment to the highest level of customer service
  • A high level of numeracy and a good understanding of financial workings
  • A keen eye for detail and a solution focused approach, able to act positively, creatively and intuitively when presented with challenges
Interested to be considered or to find out more? Please apply now or contact Becky Bradley at Balance Recruitment (beckybradley@balancerecruitment.com) to discuss further. Don't worry if you don't have your CV together yet, we can help with that.
We are an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome qualified applicants of all abilities, backgrounds, experiences and characteristics. If you require any adjustments or additional support during any stage of the recruitment process, please just let us know.

job.title: VAT Manager
job.description:
Role: VAT Manager
Salary: Up to £100,000
Location: London, in office 3 days p/wk
Contract: Permanent

Are you an experienced VAT or indirect tax compliance professional looking for a role where you can take genuine end to end ownership, rather than just being one part of a bigger process? A well established international law firm is expanding its London based indirect tax operations capability, and is looking for a VAT Manager to take charge of its day to day compliance activity across multiple jurisdictions.

The Role
Reporting to the Indirect Tax Operations Manager, the VAT Manager will own the day to day delivery of the firm's indirect tax compliance activities across multiple jurisdictions, including Europe, Asia Pacific, and the Middle East. This is a hands on role with real scope for ownership, sitting within a growing Indirect Tax Operations Team and working closely with Finance, Billing, Accounting, Accounts Payable, Financial Systems, local office personnel, and external advisors. You will also supervise and develop a VAT Analyst, giving you a genuine management dimension alongside the technical work. Key responsibilities include:
  • Managing preparation, review, and submission of VAT/GST returns across applicable jurisdictions.
  • Managing European Sales Listings, Intrastat filings, and other periodic indirect tax reporting obligations.
  • Owning the firm's VAT compliance calendar and ensuring filing deadlines and submission requirements are met.
  • Reviewing supporting workpapers, account reconciliations, data extracts, and compliance documentation prepared by the VAT Analyst or external advisors.
  • Monitoring VAT legislative and administrative developments and coordinating implementation of required filing or process updates.
  • Managing recurring interactions with external VAT advisors and service providers, and coordinating responses to tax authority inquiries and VAT audits.
  • Leading, supervising, and mentoring the VAT Analyst, setting priorities and delivering technical coaching on filings, reconciliations, and documentation.
  • Supporting e invoicing and real time reporting initiatives, and contributing to process documentation, compliance playbooks, and control improvements.
  • Supporting VAT registrations, deregistrations, and changes to existing registrations as the firm's obligations evolve.
The Candidate
We are looking for someone with:
  • 8+ years of VAT or indirect tax compliance experience, ideally within a multinational organisation, professional services firm, or law firm environment.
  • Strong practical knowledge of VAT/GST returns, European Sales Listings, Intrastat reporting, VAT registrations, and related compliance requirements.
  • Experience managing multi jurisdictional filing obligations and advisor relationships.
  • Experience supporting VAT audits, tax authority inquiries, or compliance reviews.
  • Strong Excel and data management skills, and comfort working with large datasets and reconciliations.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities across jurisdictions.
  • A proactive and solutions oriented approach, with the confidence to take ownership of day to day compliance activities and drive issues through to resolution.
  • The ability to supervise and develop less experienced team members.
  • Interest in e invoicing, tax technology, automation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • ATT, CTA, ACA, ACCA, or equivalent qualification, or progress toward qualification, is preferred but not essential.
Interested to be considered or to find out more? Please apply now or contact Becky Bradley at Balance Recruitment to discuss further. Don't worry if you don't have your CV together yet, we can help with that.

job.title: Assistant Management Accountant
job.description:
Salary: £45,000 to £55,000
Location: London (hybrid working 3 days p/wk in office)
Contract: Permanent

Are you a part qualified accountant looking to build your career within a genuinely supportive, international finance function? A well established international law firm is looking for an Assistant Management Accountant to join its London Finance team on a permanent basis.

The Role
Reporting to the London Finance Manager, you will support the head office finance team across the full management accounting cycle, working closely with department heads and senior finance personnel, while being given genuine study support towards a professional accounting qualification.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Preparation of the London office's monthly management accounts, including accruals, prepayments, bad debt provisions, the fixed asset register and interest and loan schedules.
  • Review and analysis of the monthly London P&L report, including commentary.
  • Liaising with the Accounts Payable team on correct coding of purchase invoices and expenses, and transfers between general ledger accounts.
  • Preparation of departmental management accounts packs and liaising with department heads on expenditure versus budget.
  • Preparation of monthly balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Providing ad hoc analysis and reporting on general ledger transactions as requested by department heads and senior finance staff.
  • Liaising with external auditors during the annual audit process.
  • Approving and signing off the monthly payment run, checking coding, posting and approvals.
  • Reviewing and processing recharges and inter-office debit notes for international offices.
  • Assisting with preparation of the UK quarterly VAT return.
  • Attending budget meetings with Business Services Heads and finance leadership, updating budget schedules and supporting the annual budget process.
  • Preparation of monthly and annual national statistics questionnaires.
  • Any other ad hoc duties as required.
The Candidate
We are looking for someone with:
  • A Levels or AAT (or equivalent) and a degree, with study towards a professional accounting qualification (ACCA or similar).
  • At least two years' experience working in finance within the legal sector, professional services, or audit.
  • Strong general ledger experience.
  • Experience with a practice management system such as Elite 3E is an advantage.
  • Enthusiastic, self motivated and a strong relationship builder, with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise conflicting demands.
  • High level of attention to detail with a questioning mindset and a desire to add value.

job.title: Billing and Rates Analyst
job.description:
Role: Billing and Rates Analyst
Salary: Up to £60,000
Location: London (hybrid working)
Contract: Permanent
Are you an analytical, detail focused professional with a couple of years' experience in a law firm looking for a role where accuracy and structure genuinely matter? A well established international law firm is creating a brand new role within its London office, working as part of a global finance function that supports the firm's client and matter lifecycle across its offices.
The Role
This is a newly created position for the London office, giving you the chance to help shape the role as it develops. Working closely with London based partners, and with regular touchpoints across the firm's international finance teams, the Billing and Rates Analyst will be responsible for ensuring client billing arrangements are captured, applied and maintained accurately throughout the life of a matter. Key responsibilities include:
  • Reviewing and validating client and matter financial terms to ensure completeness, accuracy and compliance with client agreements and firm policy.
  • Supporting the client intake process, reviewing financial information submitted as part of new business onboarding.
  • Configuring and maintaining financial terms within the firm's financial systems, including billing arrangements, rate structures and discounts.
  • Reviewing financial provisions within client guidelines and engagement documentation to ensure correct interpretation and consistent application.
  • Working closely with Billing, eBilling, Accounts Receivable and Pricing teams to ensure financial terms are applied consistently across the revenue cycle.
  • Supporting the onboarding of other European offices as the finance function grows.
The Candidate
We are looking for someone with:
  • Around two+ years of analytical experience, ideally gained within a law firm, Big Four firm or corporate environment.
  • A degree is preferred, but candidates with AAT or equivalent relevant accounting experience are equally encouraged to apply.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel. Experience with a legal Practice Management System, such as 3E or Intapp, would be an advantage.
  • A naturally organised, detail focused approach, with the confidence to work at pace and interpret limited instructions from busy partners.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to build relationships across a range of teams.
  • Comfort with process driven, repetitive work, balanced by the ability to work independently once familiar with the role.

job.title: Revenue Controller
job.description:
Role: Revenue Controller
Salary: Up to £58,000
Location: London (hybrid working, 3 day p/wk in office)
Contract: Permanent

Are you a high performing, detail oriented Revenue Controller looking for your next move within a well regarded law firm? A leading London based firm is seeking a proactive individual to support the financial operations of its partners and fee earners. This is a high impact role requiring initiative, accuracy and strong communication skills, playing a key part in maintaining billing momentum, improving cash flow and upholding the firm's client service standards.

The Role
Acting as the main point of contact for all revenue related activities, the Revenue Controller will work closely with partners, fee earners, LEAs, clients and the wider finance team, driving best practice in billing, collections and revenue compliance. Key responsibilities include:
  • Conducting regular WIP review meetings with partners and fee earners to drive timely invoicing, monitoring aged WIP and advising on billing best practice to avoid build up.
  • Assisting in setting monthly billing targets and forecasts based on partner input and historic trends.
  • Using 3E to prepare and issue bills, processing transfers of time and costs, narrative amends, time divides, write offs and credit notes.
  • Ensuring billing instructions and client billing details are kept up to date on matters, and assisting with distribution of completed invoices.
  • Monitoring aged debts and proactively following up on overdue invoices, communicating directly with clients to resolve outstanding payments while maintaining strong relationships.
  • Escalating payment delays or disputes to relevant stakeholders and supporting monthly collections forecasting to help meet cash flow targets.
  • Providing regular and ad hoc reporting on accounts receivable.
  • Working with the eBilling Support Team to ensure timely, accurate submission of e bills, monitoring and troubleshooting rejections and staying up to date with client specific billing guidelines.
  • Producing detailed reports on WIP, AR, collections and cash receipts through 3E.
  • Building strong working relationships with partners, fee earners, business services teams and client finance teams to ensure smooth invoice processing.
The Candidate
We are looking for a motivated Revenue Controller with:
  • Demonstrable experience in a revenue, billing or credit control role within a law firm.
  • Strong knowledge of billing systems, ideally 3E.
  • Exposure to client e billing platforms such as CounselLink or Legal Tracker.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills at all levels.
  • The ability to take ownership of tasks and work proactively on own initiative.
  • Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills.
  • The ability to prioritise multiple tasks, solve problems and work well under pressure.
  • High proficiency across MS Suite, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
